Holmes and Watson find a walking stick left behind by a visitor.
Holmes deduces from the stick that its owner is a kind country doctor with a dog.
Dr Mortimer comes to claim his stick and to ask for Holmes's help.
Mortimer reads the family manuscript about the cruel Hugo Baskerville.
Hugo locks up a farmer's daughter, but she escapes across the moor and he rides after her.
Hugo is found dead beside an enormous hound, and a curse begins to follow the family.
Sir Charles Baskerville is found dead on the yew path, and people speak of the curse.
Mortimer reveals that he saw the footprints of an enormous dog near the body.
Sir Henry arrives from Canada with a warning letter made of words cut from a newspaper.
A new brown boot and then an old black one disappear from Sir Henry's hotel.
A bearded man follows Sir Henry through London in a cab and escapes.
Holmes is too busy to leave London and sends Watson to guard Sir Henry.
At a small station the travellers learn that the convict Selden has escaped.
The travellers reach Baskerville Hall and meet Barrymore the butler and his wife.
Watson hears a woman sobbing in the night, and Mrs Barrymore's eyes are red in the morning.
Watson meets the naturalist Stapleton, who warns him about Grimpen Mire.
A long, deep howl rolls over the moor at sunset.
Beryl mistakes Watson for Sir Henry and begs him to leave Devonshire.
Sir Henry falls in love with Beryl, and Stapleton angrily tries to stop it.
Watson sees Barrymore signalling with a candle at a window facing the moor.
Barrymore confesses that the candle is a signal for Selden, his wife's brother.
Sir Henry and Watson chase Selden over the moor, but he escapes.
Watson sees a mysterious stranger standing on a rock above the moor.
A scrap of burned letter points to a woman called Laura Lyons.
Watson meets Mr Frankland, who watches the moor through a telescope.
Laura Lyons admits that she wrote to Sir Charles asking for money.
She says she never met Sir Charles, because a friend told her to stay home.
Frankland reports that a boy carries food to a hidden man on the moor.
Watson climbs the hill to search the stone huts for the hidden man.
In one hut Watson finds a camp and a note that describes his own movements.
The hidden man turns out to be Sherlock Holmes himself.
Holmes explains that he came in secret to watch the moor and the people on it.
A scream rings out in the night, and they find a body in Sir Henry's old clothes.
The dead man is Selden, and Stapleton arrives, shocked to see Holmes.
Holmes sees that Hugo's cruel face looks like Stapleton's.
Lestrade arrives, and Holmes explains a plan to catch the villain.
The three men wait near Merripit House as a thick fog creeps in.
Sir Henry leaves Merripit House and begins his walk home alone.
A huge hound with a burning mouth springs out of the fog after Sir Henry.
Holmes shoots the hound dead, and Sir Henry is safe but shaken.
The hound is revealed to be a living dog covered in glowing phosphorus.
In Merripit House they find Beryl tied up, and learn she is Stapleton's wife.
Stapleton has fled toward Grimpen Mire, and the fog hides him.
The tracks end in the Mire beside a missing boot, and Stapleton is presumed lost.
Holmes reveals that Stapleton was really a Baskerville and the next heir.
Holmes explains the hidden hound, Sir Charles's death and Selden's fall.
Sir Henry slowly recovers from the terrible night.
Sir Henry thanks his friends and leaves on a long sea voyage with Mortimer.
Holmes and Watson travel home to London, and the moor is safe again.
Back at Baker Street, Holmes suggests an evening at the opera.
